findings.expected: D2-S01 / REPAIR-D3 §2: the outcome should not be predictable from incidental coefficient patterns, only from analysing v.
findings.actual: The 28 single/pair tests reproduce (no perfect separator). But all 24 no-change tuples use c=1 and r>=4, so only 3 normalised no-change polynomials occur (t^2-3t-4, t^2-4t-5, t^2-5t-6). Consequences: |b|>=4|a| occurs only in no-change (18/24 NC, 0/144 SC); the (a,b) lookup is right 162/168, and its only overlap is b/a=-3, i.e. NC (4,1,3) versus SC (4,1,5); 'sum of roots -b/a >= T' (vertex at or right of T/2) separates 168/168; the pair (b/a, T) and 8 visible triples (all containing T and b or |b|) separate perfectly; v(0)=v(T) happens only in no-change (18/24). The naive shortcuts the brief lists give nothing: sign(d) is always opposite sign(a); d/a is always an integer; 'T > |d|/|a|' 108/168; 'T is the largest printed number' 96/168 (majority baseline 144/168). Comparing the signs of v(0) and v(T) separates 168/168, but that is a legitimate algebraic test, not a shortcut.
findings.evidence: Reviewer enumeration (scratch motion/mixed_domain.py, enum-out.json). A candidate fix, no-change contexts (4,1,3),(4,3,3),(5,2,4),(6,3,5) (margins 1), lowers the best single/pair lookup to 156/168, leaves no perfectly separating visible triple, and cuts the vertex/ratio rules to at most 156/168.
findings.repair: Diversify the no-change contexts over c in {2,3} (e.g. the set above), then re-run the separation test and the sweeps. Alternatively, disclose to Vitalis that a ratio-level pattern (c=1 only; |b|>=4|a| implies no change) remains. Judgement at the margin: a learner is unlikely to discover -b/a>=T without analysis, so this could be accepted as a disclosed note. STATUS.md:7 says D3 'removes the mixed-motion visible-parameter shortcut'; that is true only for single and pair tests.

findings.expected: Every example given in the R1 constant-sign alternative should be a valid route on the admitted domain. Invalid look-alikes should be named as earning no R1.
findings.actual: R1 cites 'endpoint signs plus appropriate concavity or a vertex bound'. In all 24 no-change tuples the vertex lies inside (0,T), and v(vertex) is the extremum on the far side from zero: a negative minimum when k>0, a positive maximum when k<0. So a vertex value never certifies constant sign (0/24). A valid 'vertex bound' (completing the square and bounding (t-t_v)^2 on [0,T]) reduces to the endpoint check. The JSON excludes only 'vertex location alone', so an argument such as 'v(3/2)=25/4>0 is the maximum, so v>0' could be given R1, then R3/R4, for 4/4 on invalid reasoning. Origin: our own D2 finding and REPAIR-D3 prompt suggested 'the vertex value' or 'vertex/minimum value' (motion-D2-03), which is invalid for this domain.
findings.evidence: Reviewer check in exemplars-out.json, vertex_argument: vertex inside 24/24; certifies 0/24. For example, (1,4,1,3): v(3/2)=-25/4 is a minimum, with v(0)=v(3)=-4.
findings.repair: Replace 'or a vertex bound' with 'or completed-square form with (t-t_v)^2 bounded on [0,T]'. Add a negative fixture: an extremum value alone, or a vertex value on the far side from zero, earns no R1.
